It's obvious from your error log, that there is infinite loop in PHP and that's why you get memory exhausted error on your server. Though I can't say whether the reason is configuration or code itself as I haven't used that functionality in Yii.

@armpogart I agree. The question is: what causes it? My site does not have the infinite loop when I don't enable e-the mail logging, so I suspect it is somehow faulty. I did not extend the standard functionality, but it might be caused by my configuration. (Maybe the fact that a lot of translations are currently missing?)
Maybe sending error through email generates another error, that is being send via email?

@docsolver To better get idea of what is causing the infinite loop, try to do the following (if not already):
1. Install empty yii2 application
2. Configure log (I don't whether that configuration is correct, as I haven't used it). Use docs example if there is any.
3. Configure yii debugger (optional). This will show more pretty stack trace and error log.
4. And simply add a line in SiteController that will trigger error (e.g. echo $something without ending line with ';')
5. Try first without except in mail error log configuration.

This way we will have correct replication of the problem as we will eliminate the possibility of any other additional code to be the reason.
Paste stack trace again here if any.
alright, I'll try that. Will keep you posted.

@nineinchnick I think the reason is the code in Yii core that must send error log as I don't see any error in Stack Trace if it is fully pasted here. Stack Trace shows only infinite loop and no any other error until the point when memory is exhausted. I even think that no any error in code at all, it simply loops while initiating error log component.

Probably when creating the email I18N is called. I18N logs an entry about missing translations. I think this could be reported as an another issue, because when a  translation is missing it should just use the original label.
@nineinchnick sounds probable. However, when I change the mail logger's level to error only (and a missing translation is not an error, right?) I also get into the infinite loop.

> Probably when creating the email I18N is called. I18N logs an entry about missing translations. I think this could be reported as an another issue, because when a translation is missing it should just use the original label.

It is exactly like that. The warning is not about missing message but about not configured tranlation category. Which is the case because we do not have translations that come with the framework yet.
A message being logged while processing logs should not cause problems so we should fix this.
Updated the title to match the problem.
Could you update and try again? Thanks.
It is fixed! Thanks for the quick response all!
